label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 10
knowledgePattern: Classify parameterised trigonometric root counts without cancelling a branch
solution:
Use 1−cos2x=sin2x and factor: sinx(sin2x−k)=0. The first branch gives x=0,π,2π, three distinct solutions for every k.

If k < 0 or k > 1, the other branch adds none. For k = 0 it repeats the same three roots. For 0 < k < 1 it adds four distinct angles. For k = 1 it adds π/2 and 3π/2.

Therefore n = 3 for k ≤ 0 or k > 1, n = 7 for 0 < k < 1, and n = 5 for k = 1. Statement I is true; II fails at k = 0; III is true. Answer D.

hints.title: Keep every zero factor
hints.body: Use the squared sine/cosine identity, move all terms to one side and factor without cancelling a trigonometric factor.
hints.recap: Factoring preserves zero branches that division could discard.
hints.pitfall: A shared root of two branches counts once, not twice.
hints.pause: Write the separate equations whose roots you must combine.

hints.title: Move the level across the full range
hints.body: For the parameter-dependent branch, use its attainable range and check boundary levels separately from interior levels.
hints.recap: Count all trigonometric branches on the transformed interval, including permitted endpoints and removing duplicates.
hints.pitfall: The separate phrases “if” and “only if” set different implication directions.
